summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Manuka Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as Australia posted 534/5 (131.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 215/10 (68.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 308-Run Stand: Travis Head & JA Burns, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Travis Head delivered a masterclass for Australia (220 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Australia 74%) and allowing Australia to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Australia's bowling unit, bolstered by Mitchell Starc (10 Wickets), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Australia won by 366 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Australia's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, Australia won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
